subject: Put a categorical covariate as a factor.

messages.author: b8b27ae22e1e4f40
messages.subject: Put a categorical covariate as a factor.
parts:
Hi everyone, I´m new in R and unmarked, so a struggling with something.

I have a categorical covariate wind going from 0 (low speed wind) to 4 (high speed wind). I´m trying to concatenate all my wind columns in one object to use it in my analysis.


I´ve tried different ways:

1.       

            1)

      wind <- data.frame(Argiope[,14:19])

2.      

            2)

      wind<-as.matrix(sapply(Argiope[,14:19], as.factor))

 

3)

3.       wind <- sapply(Argiope[,14:19], as.factor)

wind <-as.factor(wind)


However, any of these can run properly. The closest one of I want is the third option, however, as I said, it won´t run properly (It discard some observations of my occupancy).


Attached is my wind .csv. As you can see, in some samples, not all four possible wind speeds are showed and I supposed that this is the problem I´m having.


Can someone help me?

messages.author: ab7bbe167f897cdd
messages.subject: Re: Put a categorical covariate as a factor.
parts: I would bet that your suggestion about not having all four possible wind speed levels in the data could be a problem. Try something like droplevels() (http://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/base/html/droplevels.html) to reset all the possible values, or relevel() (https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/stats/html/relevel.html) in which you can also choose the reference level to be used.
